thread.title: Hot, dry summer taking toll on Missouri farms - NewsBreak

author: Jeff Bernthal
title: Hot, dry summer taking toll on Missouri farms - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeff Bernthal ,
1 hours ago
HAWK POINT, Mo. - When Colby Ruether checked on the large-scale irrigator that was watering crops on one of the Ruether Bros and Sons Farms in Hawk Point on Wednesday, he discovered a herd of cattle moving under the water spray in an apparent attempt to cool off. The extreme heat is only adding to work that never seems to end.
“It’s definitely a seven-day-a-week job,” he said. “You’re always making sure everything’s okay.”
Ruether said the extreme is taking a toll. He said livestock in the Midwest have a different tolerance for extreme heat than livestock in the South.
“They’re just not cut out for this kind of heat,” he said.
Paroled killer charged with threatening to harm coworkers in St. Charles His family’s farm also grows row crops, including corn and soybeans. This year, with the late blast of extreme heat, Ruether said his family will be harvesting crops earlier than normal because they will be unable to wait for them to fully mature.
“Whenever you don’t get any rain for a week or so, the plants all just shut down and kind of say we’re done for the year,” said Ruether.
He predicts fewer crops will result in higher prices. Ruether hopes the hard work is appreciated. He added, “I couldn’t imagine really doing anything else.”
